overview_title: What Is the Best 7-Day Guatemala Itinerary?
answer: The best 7-day Guatemala itinerary, as James Wild & Co draws it, is two nights at Villa Bokéh in Antigua, two at Casa Palopó on Lake Atitlán and two at Bolontiku on Lake Petén Itzá, for Tikal at first light. Fly into La Aurora (GUA) in Guatemala City, go by road or helicopter to the highlands, then fly about an hour to Flores (FRS) for the Petén.

days.title: Into Antigua
days.line: By road from Guatemala City · 45 minutes to 1.5 hours
days.body: Land at La Aurora International Airport (GUA) in Guatemala City. Antigua has no airport of its own; it is 45 minutes to an hour and a half away by road, depending on traffic. Villa Bokéh arranges a private transfer from the airport, and it has a helipad if you would rather fly. The estate sits about 3 km from the old centre, among gardens in the shadow of the volcanoes.
days.stageMeta: DAYS 1 TO 2 · 2 NIGHTS · THE OLD CAPITAL

days.title: The old capital
days.body: Antigua was the capital of the Captaincy-General of Guatemala until the Santa Marta earthquakes of 1773 moved it to what is now Guatemala City. What stayed is a grid of cobbled streets at about 1,500 metres, churches with low bell towers built for earthquakes, and the ruins of the ones that fell. UNESCO inscribed it in 1979. Villa Bokéh's guided walk takes in the Cathedral, La Merced and San Francisco; come back for a canoe across its lagoon, then dinner at Bokéh 3.1.

days.title: Antigua to Lake Atitlán
days.line: By road or helicopter into the highlands
days.body: To Lake Atitlán, which fills a volcanic caldera formed about 84,000 years ago, under the San Pedro, Tolimán and Atitlán volcanoes. Casa Palopó sits on the lake at Santa Catarina Palopó; it has a helipad, and Villa Bokéh and Casa Palopó are sister hotels that suggest exactly this order, Antigua first, then the lake.
days.move: By road, or helicopter between the hotels' helipads

days.title: The lake by boat
days.line: Between the Maya towns of Atitlán
days.body: Boats run from Panajachel's docks to San Marcos La Laguna, San Juan La Laguna, Santiago Atitlán and the other Maya towns on the shore. Casa Palopó's own day in San Juan La Laguna brings honey and chocolate, textile workshops and murals; at dawn there are kayaks and paddle boards, and at night a telescope for the stars over the lake.
days.acts: Lake towns by boat · San Juan La Laguna

days.title: Up to the Petén
days.line: By road, by air, then by boat
days.body: By road from Casa Palopó to Guatemala City, 3 to 3.5 hours as the hotel states (or by helicopter from its helipad), then a flight of about an hour to Flores (FRS). Bolontiku's team takes you to the municipal dock for a complimentary 10 to 15 minute boat ride across Lake Petén Itzá.
days.acts: Transfer day · a swim in the lake

days.title: Tikal at first light
days.line: Tikal National Park, just over an hour from Bolontiku
days.body: Tikal is just over an hour from Bolontiku. The park covers 57,600 hectares of forest, wetland and savannah, and UNESCO lists it for both its Maya city and its wildlife: five wild cats, howler and spider monkeys and more than 300 bird species. The city was lived in from about 600 BC until around 900 AD. Go at first light, before the heat, then back to the lake to swim, kayak or book the private temazcal.

days.title: Home through Guatemala City
days.line: By boat, then a flight of about an hour
days.body: The boat back across Lake Petén Itzá, then a flight of about an hour from Flores (FRS) to Guatemala City (GUA) for flights home.

getThere.title: Two Halves, One Short Flight Apart
getThere.intro: Guatemala is less than 500 km from north to south, but the mountain roads are slow, so the route splits it in two: the highlands by road, the Petén by air.
points: Villa Bokéh and Casa Palopó both have helipads, so James can fly the highland legs instead of driving them. Ask when you plan; flights are quoted with your dates.
Most international flights land at La Aurora, about 2.5 to 3 hours from Miami or Houston, with a direct flight from Madrid. Antigua is 45 minutes to an hour and a half away by road.
Daily flights of about an hour connect Guatemala City with Mundo Maya International Airport at Flores. Bolontiku's team meets you for a complimentary 10 to 15 minute boat ride across Lake Petén Itzá.

Villa Bokéh puts Antigua about 45 minutes from Guatemala City and arranges a private transfer. Casa Palopó puts the drive from Guatemala City at 3 to 3.5 hours, with a private transfer it coordinates. Boats cross from Panajachel's docks to the other lakeside towns.
By road, the crossing is Melchor de Mencos. Bolontiku can meet guests coming from Belize at the border, about 1 hour 35 minutes from its dock.

founder.title: The Highlands by Road, the Petén by Air
founder.p1: James has not stayed at Villa Bokéh, Casa Palopó or Bolontiku. They are filed from the hotels' own information (and the Cayuga Collection's, for Bolontiku), and the route is drawn from the house's Guatemala page and the official sources behind it: UNESCO for Tikal and Antigua.
founder.p2: Guatemala looks small on the map. It isn't, once you're on the road. So the route treats it as two trips joined by a one-hour flight: Antigua and Atitlán first, then the Petén, with two nights at the lake so Tikal gets a whole morning.

faqs: What is the best 7-day Guatemala itinerary?

Two nights at Villa Bokéh in Antigua, two at Casa Palopó on Lake Atitlán and two at Bolontiku on Lake Petén Itzá, with Tikal at first light on day six. Fly into Guatemala City (GUA), go by road or helicopter to the highlands and fly about an hour to Flores (FRS) for the Petén.
How do you get to Tikal?

Fly to Flores, then drive about 65 km, an hour to an hour and a half, to Tikal National Park; from Bolontiku it is just over an hour. UNESCO listed Tikal in 1979 for both its Maya city and its forest.
Where do we stay in Antigua and on Lake Atitlán?

Villa Bokéh in Antigua and Casa Palopó on Lake Atitlán, sister hotels that suggest this order themselves: Antigua first, then the lake. Villa Bokéh has two MICHELIN Keys and Casa Palopó one, both awarded in 2025. Bolontiku is the stay on Lake Petén Itzá.
When is the best time to visit Guatemala?

November to April, the dry season, when Tikal's trails are in better shape and the volcanoes around Lake Atitlán are clearest. May to October is the rainy season: greener and quieter, with most of the rain in the afternoon. Holy Week draws the biggest crowds, so book early.
How far is Antigua from the airport?
45 minutes to an hour and a half by road from La Aurora in Guatemala City, depending on traffic. Antigua has no airport of its own.

Yes. Belize is next door: Flores to Belize City is 3 to 4 hours by road through the Melchor de Mencos border, and Bolontiku can meet guests coming from Belize at the border. Deep Belize is the house's Belize route.
Ask James. Jícaro Island Lodge, nine casitas on a private island in Lake Nicaragua and a Cayuga Collection hotel like Bolontiku, is the suggested extension, and James plans it with you directly.
Has James stayed at these hotels?
No. Villa Bokéh, Casa Palopó and Bolontiku are filed from the hotels' own information. James says so plainly on every page where he hasn't been.
How much does this route cost?
It is quoted against your dates and travellers. James Wild & Co does not publish a fixed price for this route.
